Sent by Aaron at 12:00 - Thank you for your patience while our engineers  made partial repairs to the underground network fault in the Streatham Road SS9 area, we've now restored power to most of the affected properties. There are now only 2 properties without power, who we'll speak to directly. Our engineers are now continuing with the repairs on site. What will happen next?

This outage affects multiple areas, so locations we mention may be further away than you expect. We're arranging staff to attend ASAP, but at the same time we try to restore power remotely by redirecting electricity. It's possible your power may go on and off as we try to get as many customers back on as we can.

Once available, our engineer will head to the local substation and after checking the network, they will attempt to restore more power from there. If unsuccessful, they will work to locate the issue and make repairs, which may take longer to get the lights on.

Our staff work as quickly as they can, so you might not hear about everything we're doing but we'll always give you the clearest information we have.

It is our intention to return to make a permanent repair as soon as we can.  I'm sorry, but we can't give you a time for this at present. Please accept our sincere apologies for any inconvenience this may cause.

Steps.Message:
Sent by Talie at 20:47 - A last message from us, as we can now confirm that all power in the Heathfield TN21, Hailsham BN27 area should be back on. The issue was caused by a tree falling onto our overhead cabling, which our engineers have now diverted power around. 

Usually we would send more frequent updates, so we apologise that due to the bad weather we have been unable to text as often. Storm Boelo has impacted our network with heavy rain and high winds, and we're dealing with a larger amount of power cuts than usual. 

We know that being without power can be very worrying, so we're sorry for the outage. If your power isn't on, or if there's anything you'd like to talk to us about, call us any time on 08003163105.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
Sent by Talie at 20:35 - I wanted to reach out to say that our staff are doing everything they can to get your lights back on. Heavy rain and strong winds like we're experiencing with Storm Boelo can make things harder for our engineers, especially when trying to repair overhead cabling.

While the weather is impacting our network, damage to our cabling can still occur. Usually, this is due to trees being swayed by the wind and making contact with a cable or piece of pole mounted network equipment, like a transformer.

When this happens, it can create potentially dangerous situations, so if you spot anything wrong with our equipment or cabling, please stay away from the area and call our team on 105, pressing the option for emergencies.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
With darkness now upon us we understand that it can be unsettling to have a power cut. It may help to locate a torch and anything else you may need so you can have it to hand just in case.

If you have any concerns please do not hesitate to contact our team, but we will work to fix the problem as quickly and safely as possible. Sent by Talie at 19:28.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
Sent by Talie at 18:54 - Just another check in from us, as we know power being off for longer periods can be very disruptive, and we just wanted to help explain why it can take longer to get power restored safely during bad weather like we're having at the moment.

With high winds, our engineers cannot safely do some of the things they need to, such as climb electricity poles. Added to this, heavy rain can make it difficult to travel and access our equipment.

We want to get your power back on as quickly as we can, but the safety of our staff and customers is always our first priority, so we sometimes have to wait until the weather has improved before repairs can begin.

My team and I will continue to keep you updated.

Steps.Message:
Sent by Talie at 19:47 - We can now confirm that all but one property in the Deal CT14 area should be back on. Our engineers have diverted power around the fallen tree on our overhead cables to get the majority of customers back on. However, due to the location and complexity of the issue, we have also used temporary generators to restore power to the last of the affected properties. This will provide power until our engineers plan in and safely complete the full repair, which may take a few days.

We're really sorry for any disruption this unexpected power cut caused. If your power isn't on or there's anything you'd like to talk to us about, call us on 08003163105 which is free from landlines and mobiles.

Sent by Talie at 00:51 - Just another check in from us, as we know power being off for longer periods can be very disruptive, and we just wanted to help explain why it can take longer to get power restored safely during bad weather like we're having at the moment.

With high winds, our engineers cannot safely do some of the things they need to, such as climb electricity poles. Added to this, heavy rain can make it difficult to travel and access our equipment.

We want to get your power back on as quickly as we can, but the safety of our staff and customers is always our first priority, so we sometimes have to wait until the weather has improved before repairs can begin.

My team and I will continue to keep you updated.

Thanks for your patience today. We know a power cut can be difficult, especially in colder weather.

Many properties have gas hobs, which can still be used in a power cut for cooking, or heating water for drinks and sterilisation of baby bottles. If you have any questions or concerns, our team are always on hand to help.

Steps.Message:
We're sorry if your power is still off. Due to the high winds and heavy rain from Storm Beolo impacting our network, we're dealing with more power cuts than usual.
 
Our staff are working 24/7 to help customers and fix these problems, though due to extra reports of damage and the difficult conditions, it's taking us longer to get everything repaired and the lights back on.
 
We think it's unlikely we will be able to restore your electricity tonight. Our engineers will re-attend tomorrow and we'll update you with an updated estimated time as soon as we can in the morning. This is not the message we want to send, but we want to provide you with realistic updates so you can plan ahead.

Sent by Decasta at 19:44 - I wanted to reach out to say that our staff are doing everything they can to get your lights back on. Heavy rain and strong winds like we're experiencing with Storm Boelo can make things harder for our engineers, especially when trying to repair overhead cabling.

While the weather is impacting our network, damage to our cabling can still occur. Usually, this is due to trees being swayed by the wind and making contact with a cable or piece of pole mounted network equipment, like a transformer.

When this happens, it can create potentially dangerous situations, so if you spot anything wrong with our equipment or cabling, please stay away from the area and call our team on 105, pressing the option for emergencies.

Steps.Message:
Sent by Kevin at 16:47 - Just another check in from us, as we know power being off for longer periods can be very disruptive, and we just wanted to help explain why it can take longer to get power restored safely during bad weather like we're having at the moment.

With high winds, our engineers cannot safely do some of the things they need to, such as climb electricity poles. Added to this, heavy rain can make it difficult to travel and access our equipment.

We want to get your power back on as quickly as we can, but the safety of our staff and customers is always our first priority, so we sometimes have to wait until the weather has improved before repairs can begin.

My team and I will continue to keep you updated.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
Thanks for your patience today. We know a power cut can be difficult, especially in colder weather.

Many properties have gas hobs, which can still be used in a power cut for cooking, or heating water for drinks and sterilisation of baby bottles. The spark to ignite the hob will not work however, so if you do use it please take extra care when using other ignition sources like matches or lighters. Even in daytime, the light in your house may be low in a power cut, so only do this if you are confident it can be done safely.

If you have any questions or concerns, our team are always on hand to help.

Steps.Message: Hi, I'm Ebony and I am the manager of the text messaging team at UK Power Networks in Ipswich. Today's power cut was unexpected, so we were unable to provide you with prior notice to help you plan ahead. I am pleased to confirm that we managed to resolve this by repairing a grounded overhead cable to get your lights back on as soon as possible. Just so you know, we text customers when we are made aware of problems like this, so if you would like to be notified in the future you can do so here https://UKPN.short.gy/SMS This was a widespread problem on the overhead network and I personally apologise for any disruption this has caused to your day. If you have any questions or are still without power, please call us on 105.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
Sent by Lisa at 20:37 - A last message from us, as we can now confirm that all power in the Holt NR25 area should be back on. The issue was caused by a grounded overhead cable, which our engineers have now repaired and restored power. 

Usually we would send more frequent updates, so we apologise that due to the bad weather we have been unable to text as often. The bad weather has impacted our network and we're dealing with a larger amount of power cuts than usual. 

We know that being without power can be very worrying, so we're sorry for the outage. If your power isn't on, or if there's anything you'd like to talk to us about, call us any time on 08003163105.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message: Thanks for bearing with us during the power cut today, our staff will work to restore your power as quickly and as safely as possible. A lot of our customers have questions regarding power cuts, and though you can always reach our team, you can also find some helpful information and answers to some of our most frequently asked questions on our website here - https://UKPN.short.gy/FAQ - Bear in mind this will use your mobile data, so feel free to speak to us if you'd prefer. We'll be in touch again once we have more information from our staff.

Steps.Message:
With darkness now upon us we understand that it can be unsettling to have a power cut. It may help to locate a torch and anything else you may need so you can have it to hand just in case.

If you have any concerns please do not hesitate to contact our team, but we will work to fix the problem as quickly and safely as possible. Sent by Bev at 19:03.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
Sent by Talie at 18:17 - Just another check in from us, as we know power being off for longer periods can be very disruptive, and we just wanted to help explain why it can take longer to get power restored safely during bad weather like we're having at the moment.

With high winds, our engineers cannot safely do some of the things they need to, such as climb electricity poles. Added to this, heavy rain can make it difficult to travel and access our equipment.

We want to get your power back on as quickly as we can, but the safety of our staff and customers is always our first priority, so we sometimes have to wait until the weather has improved before repairs can begin.

My team and I will continue to keep you updated.

While the weather is impacting our network, damage to our cabling can still occur. Usually, this is due to trees being swayed by the wind and making contact with a cable or piece of pole mounted network equipment, like a transformer.

When this happens, it can create potentially dangerous situations, so if you spot anything wrong with our equipment or cabling, please stay away from the area and call our team on 105, pressing the option for emergencies.

Sent by Will at 23:09 - Our engineers are on their way. At this point we think the issue is an underground network fault affecting 182 properties.

We'll keep you updated with our progress.

Steps.Message:
What will happen next?

This outage affects multiple areas, so locations we mention may be further away than you expect. We're arranging staff to attend ASAP, but at the same time we try to restore power remotely by redirecting electricity. It's possible your power may go on and off as we try to get as many customers back on as we can.

Once available, our engineer will head to the local substation and after checking the network, they will attempt to restore more power from there. If unsuccessful, they will work to locate the issue and make repairs, which may take longer to get the lights on.

Our staff work as quickly as they can, so you might not hear about everything we're doing but we'll always give you the clearest information we have.
